title: Best Beat Makers (2026): How to Buy or Commission Beats
description: How to hire a beat maker or buy beats online: leasing versus exclusive rights, files, how to brief it, what drives the price and red flags.
intro: Beat makers produce instrumentals for rappers, singers and content creators, in genres like hip-hop, trap, R&B, pop and lo-fi. You can lease an existing beat or commission a custom one. Problems usually come from licenses: leases with limits you did not read, beats sold as exclusive more than once, or samples that were never cleared. This guide helps you get beats you can safely release.

faq.q: What is the difference between leasing and buying exclusive rights?
faq.a: A lease lets you use a beat under certain limits, such as a number of streams or copies, while the producer can lease it to others. Exclusive rights usually mean the beat is sold only to you. Read the terms carefully.
If you want a mix engineer to balance your vocals with the beat, stems help a lot. Many leases include only a stereo file; stems may cost extra.

faq.q: What about samples in the beat?
faq.a: Beats that use samples from other recordings need clearance before commercial release. Ask whether the beat contains any uncleared samples.

faq.q: Do producers get credit or royalties?
faq.a: Often a producer credit, and sometimes a share of royalties or publishing. Agree in writing.

faq.q: Can I get a custom beat made for my song?
faq.a: Yes. Custom beats are made to your brief, often with more say in structure and sound.
